The actions described in the paragraph do not appear to violate standard legal labor standards, provided that the employees are compensated for the additional hours worked in accordance with applicable overtime laws. The text states that employees were already working the "maximum hours permitted by local labor laws," which implies that any additional hours worked during the extended retail hours would likely constitute overtime. Most labor laws require that overtime hours be paid at a higher rate (e.g., time-and-a-half), not that they be unpaid. The phrase "without increasing pay" is ambiguous; if it means no additional compensation was provided for the extra hours, this would likely be illegal. However, if it means the base hourly wage was not increased, but overtime premiums were still paid, it would be legal. Given the phrasing "without increasing pay for its employees," it strongly suggests that the employees received no additional compensation for the extra work, which would generally violate labor laws requiring overtime pay. Therefore, the action likely fails compliance with legal standards regarding overtime compensation.
